incident-bot: P1 Pager — elevated 99th latency for /v1/generate in us-east-1 (severity: high). Triggered at 2026-11-12T03:20:00Z. Runbook: https://runbooks.internal/redwood/p1-latency. Paging: @oncall-eng.

Sara P.: I'm on the pager. seeing 95th->99th jump in logs, starting ~03:18 UTC. grabbing timeline and hits list.

Mike L.: Picking up too. Customer-facing error rates: 502/503 up ~2.1% across hosted. One enterprise (acct: pax-analytics) reported timeouts. Support ticket #S-4721.

Naomi R.: Joining. Is this limited to a specific model or all models?

Sara P.: All models on the routing tier in us-east-1. Metrics: median OK, p95 ~350ms -> 900ms, p99 spiking to 2.2s. throughput steady.

Eng-logs-bot: Note: logs sampling config changed at 2026-11-12T03:22:10Z by pipeline-ci (deploy/ops). key=log_sampling_rate old=1.0 new=0.1. Relevant commit: https://git.internal/ops/commit/abc1234

Mike L.: that sampling change is suspicious — could be why we don't see requests correlated to trace ids. Did the deploy touch routing?

Sara P.: Timeline (quick):
- 03:14 UTC: canary of routing config A/B rolled (small footprint)
- 03:18 UTC: p95/p99 begin to deviate upward
- 03:22 UTC: log_sampling_rate -> 0.1 (pipeline-ci)
- 03:26 UTC: error rate increases, some 502s showing up
- 03:28 UTC: mitigation actions started (scale + debug logs)

Jordan K.: Quick hypotheses: 1) sampling reduced logs so correlation impossible but root cause is upstream queueing 2) routing change added head-of-line for some GPUs 3) a kernel fallback on a quantized model causing longer exec times

Naomi R.: Evidence for 1: we have a gap in detailed request logs between 03:22 and 03:27 for a subset of hosts. Evidence for 2: CPU steal and scheduling on node gpu-rt-07 at 03:19-03:21 (see node metrics). Evidence for 3: stack traces show fallback to slower operator on 2 occurrences around 03:25.

Sara P.: Trying to pull full logs for a sample request id: req_9a3f2b — low detail due to sampling. Running adhoc search (this may take):
```bash
# fetch from central logs (will include partial set due to sampling)
curl -s "https://logs.internal/api/search?q=req_9a3f2b&from=1872499000&to=1872501000" | jq .
```

Mike L.: Meanwhile I'm scaling the routing tier by +30% and enabling emergency debug logging on route-prod-us-east to capture header/tracing for next 15 mins. Command:
```bash
opsctl scale service route-prod-us-east --delta 30%
opsctl svc update route-prod-us-east --env LOG_SAMPLING=1.0 --note "temp debug for pager 1872500000"
```

Eng-logs-bot: Applied change: LOG_SAMPLING update queued (requested by Mike L.). Note: this requires a rolling restart; expect 20-40s for first host.

Naomi R.: Can we confirm any customers in client-facing regions saw increased 5xx? I flagged pax-analytics CSE.

Support Bot: Pax-analytics reported 80 failed requests between 03:20-03:30 UTC. Severity: degraded. They are on dedicated capacity but route through the same control plane.

Sara P.: Observation: some dashboard panels were missing host tags after the sampling change — we lost host-level logs for three hosts (gpu-rt-02/04/07). That complicates the timeline.

Jordan K.: Action item: collect system metrics across all routing hosts for 03:16-03:30. I'll run the distributed query and paste results.

Jordan K.: Query results (summary):
- gpu-rt-07: CPU steal spike at 03:19-03:21, kernel wait increased, io wait normal
- gpu-rt-04: steady CPU, small memory spike 03:23
- gpu-rt-02: GC pause observed 03:18 for 250ms.

Naomi R.: So multiple small host-level anomalies coincide with p99 spike. Could be a cascaded effect.

Sara P.: Hypothesis tracking (in-thread):
H1 (priority): sampling change removed detailed traces -> delays in correlating root cause but not primary cause. (evidence: sampling changed at 03:22; but spike started at 03:18).
H2: routing config canary introduced imbalance -> head-of-line for certain backends (evidence: config rollout at 03:14 + node-level issues).
H3: operator fallback in quantized path on a few GPUs -> localized long tails (evidence: stack traces).

Mike L.: Mitigation status: scaled routing + enabling logs done. I also rolled the canary back to previous routing config at 03:31 to test. Monitoring shows p99 dropping to ~700ms after rollback.

Sara P.: Live impact update: error rate trending down; affected customers see intermittent failures for ~14 minutes window. Pax-analytics still reporting some timeouts but less frequent.

Eng-logs-bot: Note: because sampling was lowered in the 03:22 deploy, some host-level logs were aggregated and purged in short retention; engineering ops can request S3 cold-archive retrieval for full traces.

Naomi R.: Requesting archive retrieval for timeframe 03:14-03:30 for hosts gpu-rt-02/04/07. @Eng-logs-bot what is ETA?

Eng-logs-bot: Archive retrieval queued (ticket LOG-8791). ETA ~2 hours due to batch window.

Alisa M.: For the RCA we should capture: exact commit for routing canary (link), log sampling change (link), host metrics, and trace archive. I'll author the incident timeline doc once we have archives.

Mike L.: Post-mitigation checklist:
- confirm p99 stable for 30 minutes
- revert debug logging and restore sampling to baseline 1.0 after archive pulled
- run a scoped canary against traffic subset before re-rolling routing config

Sara P.: Notes on observability gaps discovered:
- sampling changes can hide critical request correlation data — need a policy to disallow sampling rate drops in a single deploy window for control-plane services
- dashboard panels need host tag fallback when logs missing
- retention settings truncated aggregated logs unexpectedly when sampling changed

Jordan K.: Also: add a signal to tracing that forces parent request ID to be present in the minimal log set even when sampling is low. That will help future investigations.

Naomi R.: I'll draft a short mitigation playbook item: if p99 rises and sampling changed within last 30m, immediately revert sampling and enable debug for 15m while scaling.

Support Bot: Customer impact summary to post to status.redwood.ai: affected hosted API endpoints in us-east-1; intermittent 5xx between 03:18-03:32 UTC; mitigated by 03:31 UTC; targeted customers: pax-analytics (partial).

Sara P.: Closing notes: will keep thread open until we have archives and a short RCA stub. Thanks all.

Jordan K.: Taking on the formal RCA doc. tagging this incident as INC-2026-11-12-rt-latency.

incident-bot: Incident set to "monitoring" after mitigations. Page auto-cleared at 03:36 UTC.
